chunks: From what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about what the deceased is shrouded in. He said: "Three garments. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was only shrouded in three garments: two Ṣuḥārī garments and one ḥibarah garment. The Ṣuḥārī garment is found in al-Yamāmah. And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was shrouded in three garments."

key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person to be prepared for burial
key_terms.الْيَمَامَةِ: the region identified as the place where Ṣuḥārī cloth is found
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَثْوَابٍ: three garments used as the prescribed shroud
key_terms.حِبَرَةٍ: a patterned or fine Yemeni-style garment used here as part of the shroud
key_terms.صُحَارِيَّيْنِ: two garments of the Ṣuḥārī type, a known cloth associated with al-Yamāmah
key_terms.كُفِّنَ: was shrouded; was wrapped in burial cloth
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: is shrouded; wrapped in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: How many garments should a deceased Muslim be shrouded in according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling that the deceased is shrouded in three garments. It supports this practice by citing the shrouding of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, thus grounding the ruling in established sunnah (prophetic tradition) and Imamī practice.
